reading: Ice versus water is the biggest switch. For 58 of 85 genomes the main axis of within-genome variation separates ice from water, more than winter (14) or pool (13). After dosing, ice and water states differ significantly in 53 of 60 testable genomes in 2024-25 and 45 of 47 in 2025-26. The same population behaves differently in brine than in the water below.

Sulfurimonas differs between pools, but not because of diesel. semibin_088 has one of the strongest pool separations (R² 0.45), yet the diesel-pool water moved less from its own pre-dosing state than the control did (shift 0.4×). The pools carry different strains of this genome (see Sulfur & hydrogen), which this method cannot tell apart from physiology. Along PC1 it trades ribosomal proteins (r +0.92) against motility and chemotaxis (r -0.94), and it slides from the growth end to the motile end through the 2025-26 season in both pools (growth index 98→38‰ diesel, 115→27‰ control).

Cycloclasticus lorbin_184 winds down its hydrocarbon genes as its bloom ages. Its PC1 rises with time in the 2025-26 diesel pool (r +0.66 with day). Moving up PC1, hydrocarbon-degradation genes (r -0.79) and storage (r -0.58) lose share and chaperones and proteases gain it (r +0.57). Its growth index falls (67→44‰). This is the pattern of a population running down its substrate and coping with protein stress, not of a fresh bloom.

The 2024-25 Cycloclasticus (metabat_9342) moves between growth and scavenging. Its PC1 sets ribosomal proteins (r +0.90) and cold-shock proteins (r +0.77) against motility (r -0.77), transporters (r -0.64), storage (r -0.65) and nitrogen acquisition (r -0.59): a fast-growth state versus a foraging, nutrient-limited state.

50-400-T64 is still in growth mode at the end. Its growth index rises slightly over the 2025-26 diesel season (69→81‰), consistent with its late bloom (see the 50-400-T64 page). Its main axis pairs chaperones (r +0.74), oxidative-stress (r +0.68) and cold-shock genes against transporters (r -0.67) and nitrogen acquisition (r -0.58).

Background heterotrophs slow down in the diesel pool. Two abundant genomes that do not eat diesel lose growth-index share in the diesel pool but not in the control in 2025-26: Sulfitobacter metabat_5376 (137→96‰ diesel, 160→157‰ control; shift 2.3×, R² 0.12, q = 0.0014) and UBA9145 vamb_4149 (81→52‰ diesel, 74→80‰ control). In UBA9145, phage-shock (psp) genes run opposite to PC1 (r -0.77), the same envelope-stress response seen on the Metals & toxicity page.

What this cannot do. Genomes that are abundant in only one pool (the blooming Cycloclasticus and 50-400-T64) cannot be compared between pools, because the control has too few reads on them. A MAG can hide several strains, and different strains in different pools or winters look like different states. Nitrosopumilus had too few reads for a profile. One pool per treatment, so no test separates diesel from other pool differences.
